title: Health and Well-Being Education
summary: Health and well-being are at the core of our mission to ensure that young people with disabilities live healthy, informed, and empowered lives.
problem: Young people with disabilities often face inaccessible health information, stigma, and service barriers in sexual, reproductive, menstrual, and mental health.
activities: Co-designed SRHR and menstrual health dialogues
University peer support and wellness coaching
Digital awareness campaigns and inclusive outreach
outcomes: Integration of mental health into programming
howToJoin: Register through the Get Involved form
Join peer dialogues and campaign workshops
Partner as a health service provider

title: Economic Empowerment and Livelihood Skills
summary: Economic independence is essential for dignity and self-reliance. Our programs equip young people with disabilities with practical skills, financial knowledge, and opportunities to build sustainable livelihoods.
problem: Youth with disabilities face barriers to training, finance, and markets that limit their ability to earn and save with confidence.
activities: KAZO Special Persons with Disabilities initiative
Kansanga entrepreneurship and refugee settlement support
outcomes: Inclusion of women, youth, and refugees
howToJoin: Reach out via our contact page

title: Policy Advocacy and Social Inclusion
summary: Creating lasting change requires transforming systems and attitudes through evidence-based advocacy, partnerships, and youth leadership.
problem: Systems remain inaccessible and exclusionary unless they are actively shaped by young people with disabilities and inclusive policy voices.

sections.title: Advocacy mission
sections.description: We advance rights and inclusion by centering youth leadership in policy discussions, campaigns, and systems change.

title: Talent Development and Capacity Building
summary: We focus on mentorship, creativity, confidence-building, exposure, and opportunity for young talent with disabilities.
problem: Young creatives and performers with disabilities often lack platforms, mentorship, and visibility to grow.
